channel.title: The Local France - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local France (thelocal.fr)

item.title: French PM forces final budget through parliament
item.description: French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu forced his budget through parliament without a vote for the third and final time Friday, exposing him to yet another no-confidence motion.

item.title: Top tips for furnishing your French home
item.description: From brocantes to house-clearances, trocs to Emmaüs, France has a wide variety of places selling old furniture that will give your French home that perfect 'shabby chic' look - and also save you some money.

item.title: French expression of the day: Nature peinture
item.description: It has little to do with painting and a lot to do with being natural.

item.title: La Chandeleur: Why do the French eat crêpes on February 2nd?
item.description: It's La Chandeleur on Monday - the day when France goes pancake mad. Before you start cooking up your crêpes, take a moment to learn about the history (and superstitions) surrounding this French tradition.

item.title: France extends flu and Covid vaccination campaign
item.description: The joint vaccination campaign against flu and Covid-19 was scheduled to end on January 31st - but as the viruses are still circulating throughout the country, the campaign has been extended.

item.title: Is that a crêpe or a galette? The great Breton debate
item.description: It might seem obvious, crêpes are sweet and galettes are savoury, right? But if you're in Brittany, things get a lot more complicated.

item.title: Péter: the French word that can mean farting, breaking, being drunk and more
item.description: The French verb péter means either to burst or to fart - but it also appears in dozens of idioms covering everything from boasting to being drunk, via a violent temper.

item.title: How Paris has transformed itself into a ‘post-car’ city
item.description: It has taken more than 20 years and involved numerous battles both legal and political, but Paris leaders have largely succeeded in their stated goal of limiting and reversing the car’s influence on the French capital. Here's how they did it.

item.title: French eyewear maker in spotlight after presidential showing
item.description: The aviator sunglasses that captured the world's attention when French President Emmanuel Macron wore a pair on stage in Davos in a faceoff with US counterpart Donald Trump have become an unexpected success.

item.title: Moving to France: Rural internet, driving licences and the reception for Americans
item.description: In this month's moving to France newsletter, we look at the realities of life in rural France and getting the correct visa, via internet access and why so many Americans moved to France in 2025.
